details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:68-75 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Untrusted pull-request data is interpolated directly into the inline shell command in the readiness step, enabling shell injection from a malicious branch name.
  WHY: actionlint and CI already flagged the exact `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` interpolation as untrusted, so PR-author-controlled text reaches bash syntax on the runner.
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:48-48 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The job-level `if:` decision uses attacker-controlled branch data to gate workflow execution.
  WHY: It is a trust-boundary violation even though the expression engine, not a shell, evaluates it.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:35-278 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The auto-close keyword lint matches quoted historical examples like `Fixes #2734` in the PR body and commit messages, so the PR fails its own enforcement check.
  WHY: CI confirmed the lint reports violations on the example text rather than only on real auto-close directives, blocking the fix PR itself.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:190-190 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The issue-lookup cache is per-process only and there is no rate-limit guard around repeated `gh issue view` calls.
  WHY: Concurrent runs can hit GitHub secondary rate limits and intermittently fail.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:79-170 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The archival lint is tied to a rigid `de-scoped phases` heading, so clear de-scoping prose with other headings is still rejected.
  WHY: The regex enforces a brittle literal contract rather than the stated intent to require explicit scope-gap acknowledgement.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:210-210 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The lint issues one `gh issue view` call per issue reference even when the same issue is repeated.
  WHY: Duplicate references waste API budget and increase rate-limit pressure without adding signal.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:45-150 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Blank checklist items like `- [ ]` are skipped because the checkbox regex requires non-empty text.
  WHY: Those items are omitted from the total and unchecked counts, so readiness can be undercounted.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:120-156 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: A tracking issue with zero parsed checkboxes is treated as a neutral success, so the readiness gate can pass with no signal.
  WHY: The script posts success instead of failing closed when parsing finds no checkboxes, allowing an incomplete integration PR to merge.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3383-3396 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The 3-way merge cat-file handling fabricates an empty base on failure and leaves int/main failures unhandled, so merge-file can run with missing or stale inputs.
  WHY: A cat-file failure is turned into an empty or residual tmpfile instead of aborting or skipping, which can silently produce incorrect merge results.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3393-3399 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: If `git add` fails after the merged file is copied into the worktree, the file stays modified but unstaged and the refresh commit misses it.
  WHY: The script only warns, so the committed state diverges from the working tree and later poll iterations can loop on the dirty file.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3349-3425 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `rm -rf` cleanup failures are ignored, so merge tmpdirs can be orphaned.
  WHY: A persistent cleanup failure would accumulate temp directories over long-running polling.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:8589-8600 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The completeness gate only treats `.status == "not_created"` as incomplete, so dispatched sub-issues stuck in other non-complete states can still pass.
  WHY: That narrower filter can mark the project complete prematurely even when sub-issues remain active or pending.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3330, 8589 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new variable and counter names are not anchored by a contract comment or test-name convention, so future renames can break the post-refresh behavior tests.
  WHY: The unit tests rely on exact string matches, so renaming without updating them would silently break the contract.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:3855-3891 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The auto-generated PR body is constructed in two places, so the pre-flight lint body and the submitted `gh pr create --body` text can drift.
  WHY: A future edit to only one string could let the lint pass on a body that differs from the one actually posted.
- .github/workflows/lint-pr-body-auto-close.yml:65-70 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Commit messages are fetched and piped into the lint step without explicit sanitization.
  WHY: Author-controlled commit text can still carry control characters or newlines through the shell pipeline.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:69-71 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` is interpolated directly into an inline shell command, and the same step also passes `head.sha` and `repo` inline.
  WHY: GitHub actionlint flagged the exact interpolation as untrusted, so a PR-author-controlled ref can reach shell syntax on the runner.
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:48-48 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'orchestrator/project-')` uses untrusted PR branch data in a workflow decision.
  WHY: It is still a trust-boundary violation even though the expression engine is evaluating it rather than a shell.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:60-67, 170-179 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The auto-close regex matches quoted historical text like `Fixes #2734` in the PR body and commit messages.
  WHY: CI confirmed the lint blocks the PR on example text rather than only on real auto-close directives, so the fix PR fails its own check.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3394-3396 | severity=high | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The three `git cat-file -p` calls for the 3-way merge have inconsistent error handling, with the base falling back to an empty file and int/main having no fallback.
  WHY: If `git cat-file` fails, the merge can silently lose the true merge input or reuse stale tmpfile contents and produce an incorrect result.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml:3855-3862, 3890-3891 | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The PR body string is built in two places, so the pre-flight lint body and the submitted `gh pr create --body` text can drift.
  WHY: A future edit to only one string could let the lint pass on a body that differs from the one actually posted.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3401-3402 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: If `git add` fails after `cp` succeeds, the merged file stays in the working tree but is not staged for the refresh commit.
  WHY: The script only warns and makes no attempt to restore the original content, leaving a dirty tree that never gets committed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3422-3422 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: `rm -rf "${merge_tmpdir}" 2>/dev/null || true` swallows cleanup failures.
  WHY: Orphaned temp directories can accumulate over repeated polling if cleanup keeps failing.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:68-72 | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The workflow interpolates `github.event.pull_request.head.ref` and `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` directly into an inline shell command.
  WHY: The CI actionlint check explicitly flags this as a shell-injection risk from attacker-controlled branch data.
- .github/workflows/integration-pr-readiness.yml:48-48 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The job-level conditional `if: startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'orchestrator/project-')` uses untrusted PR data for execution decisions.
  WHY: It makes workflow behavior depend on attacker-controlled branch names.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:35-278 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The auto-close keyword regex matches quoted historical text like `Fixes #2734` inside documentation and commit messages.
  WHY: The lint cannot distinguish an actual auto-close directive from prose quoting the incident, so the preventive-fix PR blocks itself.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:135-170 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The archival lint requires an exact `## De-scoped phases` heading to recognize de-scoping.
  WHY: Clear de-scoping explanations with different wording are rejected even when the intent is explicit.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:120-150 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: A tracking issue with zero parsed checkboxes is treated as a neutral success.
  WHY: Malformed or differently formatted tracking issues can let an incomplete integration PR merge because the readiness check passes vacuously.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:190-190 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The lookup cache is per-process only and the script does not rate-limit `gh issue view` calls.
  WHY: Concurrent workflow runs can exceed GitHub secondary rate limits and fail intermittently.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3383-3388 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A failed `git cat-file` for the base file falls back to an empty base file.
  WHY: `git merge-file` then merges against a zero-byte ancestor, silently degrading the 3-way merge into an unsafe path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3393-3399 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If `git merge-file` succeeds but `git add` fails after copying the merged file, the working tree remains modified without being staged.
  WHY: The refresh commit misses the change and the caller is only warned on stderr.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:120-150 | severity=medium | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: A checkbox line like `- [ ]` with no text is skipped entirely by the regex.
  WHY: Under-counting unchecked items can make readiness pass prematurely.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:210-210 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The archival lint issues one `gh issue view` call per `#N` occurrence even when the same issue is repeated.
  WHY: Repeated references consume unnecessary API budget and increase rate-limit pressure.
